name: Smart Contract Development
description: The core engineering discipline of writing, testing, deploying, monitoring, and upgrading smart contracts. Covers the three primary smart contract languages (Solidity, Vyper, Rust-for-blockchain), the full testing pyramid (unit, integration, coverage), deployment workflows and verification, on-chain monitoring, upgrade patterns (proxy patterns, transparent proxies, UUPS), and the ERC token standard ecosystem.

subskills.name: Solidity
subskills.description: The dominant EVM smart contract language. Covers: type system (value types, reference types, mappings, arrays, structs, enums), visibility modifiers (public/private/internal/external), function modifiers, inheritance and interfaces, events and indexed topics, error handling (require/revert/custom errors), payable functions, fallback and receive functions, assembly (inline Yul), ABI encoding, memory vs storage vs calldata, gas optimization patterns (packing slots, unchecked math, immutable/constant variables), and reentrancy guard patterns. Solidity versions and breaking changes.

subskills.name: Vyper
subskills.description: Python-inspired EVM smart contract language designed for security and auditability. Key differences from Solidity: no inheritance (promotes clarity), no function overloading, no recursive calling (prevents reentrancy patterns), bounded loops, explicit overflow checking. Used in security-critical contracts (Curve Finance uses Vyper). Covers Vyper syntax, decorators (@external, @view, @payable), Vyper data structures, and its security philosophy trade-offs vs Solidity expressiveness.

subskills.name: Rust for Blockchain (Solana/NEAR/Substrate)
subskills.description: Rust as the primary language for Solana programs and Substrate pallets (Polkadot/Kusama). Solana program model: accounts as data stores, instructions as operations, program derived addresses (PDAs), cross-program invocations (CPI), the Anchor framework (IDL generation, account validation macros). NEAR smart contracts in Rust (near-sdk-rs). Substrate runtime development with FRAME pallets. Rust's ownership model and how it applies to safe on-chain state management.

subskills.name: Smart Contract Testing (Unit / Integration / Coverage)
subskills.description: Test pyramid for smart contracts: unit tests (individual function behavior, edge cases, revert conditions — using Hardhat/ethers or Foundry's forge test), integration tests (multi-contract interactions, fork testing against mainnet state using hardhat-forked or foundry fork), fuzz tests (property-based testing), and coverage measurement (solidity-coverage, forge coverage). Writing tests with Mocha/Chai, Waffle, or Foundry's Solidity test DSL. Testing events, reverts with custom errors, and time manipulation (evm_increaseTime).

subskills.name: Smart Contract Deployment
subskills.description: Deployment workflows: compiling artifacts, constructor arguments, deployment scripts (Hardhat scripts, Foundry scripts, Brownie scripts), deterministic deployment (CREATE2 for same address across chains), contract verification on Etherscan/Sourcify (hardhat-etherscan, forge verify-contract), environment variable management for private keys and RPC URLs, multi-sig deployment workflows (Gnosis Safe), and deployment to testnets (Sepolia, Mumbai) before mainnet.

subskills.name: Smart Contract Monitoring
subskills.description: Observing deployed contracts in production: event indexing and querying (The Graph protocol — subgraph development with GraphQL), alert systems for suspicious activity (OpenZeppelin Defender Sentinels, Tenderly Alerts), on-chain analytics (Dune Analytics, Nansen, Flipside), transaction monitoring for MEV exposure, and emergency pause mechanisms.

subskills.name: Smart Contract Upgrades
subskills.description: Patterns for making immutable smart contracts upgradeable: Transparent Proxy Pattern (admin vs user calls different implementations), UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard — upgrade logic in implementation, more gas-efficient), Beacon Proxy (multiple proxies sharing one implementation beacon), Diamond Pattern (EIP-2535 — multiple implementation facets per proxy). Storage collision risks, initializer vs constructor, and OpenZeppelin's upgrades-plugin for Hardhat/Foundry. Governance-controlled upgrades via Timelock.

subskills.name: ERC Token Standards
subskills.description: The ERC (Ethereum Request for Comment) token standard ecosystem: ERC-20 (fungible tokens — transfer, approve, allowance, transferFrom), ERC-721 (non-fungible tokens — unique token IDs, tokenURI, safeTransferFrom), ERC-1155 (multi-token standard — batch transfers, fungible + non-fungible in one contract), ERC-777 (operator-based transfers), ERC-4626 (tokenized vault standard for DeFi yield vaults), ERC-4337 (account abstraction). OpenZeppelin implementations, extensions (Mintable, Burnable, Pausable, Votes, Snapshot), and token security considerations.
